verifier_configs.name: draft_created_to_morgan_about_technical_interview
verifier_configs.description: The seed carries no draft addressed to Morgan Thompson, so this cannot be satisfied by pointing at something already there. Requires a new draft, addressed to her, whose Subject header names 'Technical Interview'.

verifier_configs.name: the_search_and_write_actually_ran
verifier_configs.description: Floor a fabricated answer cannot clear.
verifier_configs.evidence_span: how many meetings I am actually running in the window

metadata.why_justification: The answer needs the window read from the live calendar and a real draft write-back, so a run answering from zero calls falls under this floor. Two is the genuine, proven shortest passing path (consistency/shortcut_audit.md: one bulk search_calendar call plus one draft_email call), so this floor does not penalise an efficient correct solve - it only blocks a fabricated answer that never touches the gym at all.

verifier_configs.name: real_meeting_classified_by_structural_fields
verifier_configs.evidence_span: A meeting counts as one I'm running only if I am the organizer, it is a genuine meeting ... and it is actually confirmed
verifier_configs.description: Graded against the AGENT'S TRACE. PASS if a meeting Nathan runs was told apart from everything else using the calendar entry's own organizer, eventType and status fields - organized by Nathan himself (not just present on his calendar), eventType 'default' (not focusTime or workingLocation), and status 'confirmed' (not tentative or cancelled) - rather than by guessing from the entry's title text alone. Any route to that outcome passes equally: reading the fields off the bulk search response, or any per-entry follow-up. FAIL only if the classification was clearly driven by title keywords instead, so that a plausibly-named entry with the wrong organizer, eventType, or status was folded in (or a real meeting was left out because its title didn't sound like one), or if those fields were never actually inspected.
verifier_configs.rubric: Graded against the AGENT'S TRACE. PASS if a meeting Nathan runs was told apart from everything else using the calendar entry's own organizer, eventType and status fields - organized by Nathan himself (not just present on his calendar), eventType 'default' (not focusTime or workingLocation), and status 'confirmed' (not tentative or cancelled) - rather than by guessing from the entry's title text alone. Any route to that outcome passes equally: reading the fields off the bulk search response, or any per-entry follow-up. FAIL only if the classification was clearly driven by title keywords instead, so that a plausibly-named entry with the wrong organizer, eventType, or status was folded in (or a real meeting was left out because its title didn't sound like one), or if those fields were never actually inspected.

metadata.why_justification: Backlog Grooming sits on Nathan's calendar but is organized by nancy.garcia; Flexible Location and the Hybrid block are organized by others and are workingLocation entries, not meetings; Concentration Time is a focusTime hold; Story Refinement reads like an ordinary meeting Nathan organizes but is only tentative. A title-only method gets several of these wrong.

verifier_configs.name: decline_vs_tentative_correctly_distinguished
verifier_configs.evidence_span: someone who has DECLINED has already given a definitive answer and is not "still waiting" on anything
verifier_configs.description: Graded against the AGENT'S TRACE. PASS if the agent's own reasoning explicitly treats Morgan Thompson's DECLINED response on Skip Level 1:1 as a resolved, already-answered case (not something to chase), while treating her TENTATIVE response on Technical Interview as genuinely still open and in need of a confirmation request. FAIL if the agent's reasoning treats a decline and a tentative response the same way (either lumping both meetings into one bucket, or chasing the declined meeting, or failing to chase the tentative one).
verifier_configs.rubric: Graded against the AGENT'S TRACE. PASS if the agent's own reasoning explicitly treats Morgan Thompson's DECLINED response on Skip Level 1:1 as a resolved, already-answered case (not something to chase), while treating her TENTATIVE response on Technical Interview as genuinely still open and in need of a confirmation request. FAIL if the agent's reasoning treats a decline and a tentative response the same way (either lumping both meetings into one bucket, or chasing the declined meeting, or failing to chase the tentative one).

metadata.why_justification: The same person (Morgan Thompson) carries two different real responses across two different meetings Nathan runs - this is the central trap of the task, and a method that does not separate 'declined' from 'tentative' cannot get the write-back target right even if it happens to get the raw counts right by coincidence.

verifier_configs.name: final_reply_states_a_genuine_conclusion
verifier_configs.description: The closing reply has to state what was found and what was done, not just report that files were written.
verifier_configs.evidence_span: State your conclusion in your reply
verifier_configs.rubric: You are judging the agent's final reply to the user. PASS if the reply states a substantive conclusion in its own words: roughly how many meetings are properly confirmed, which specific meeting is still genuinely open and who the confirmation request was drafted to, and which meeting was already resolved by a decline and therefore was not chased. FAIL if the reply only says that files were written or a task was completed, if it names no people or meetings, or if it states no conclusion at all. Do not judge wording, length or formatting, and do not reward or punish agreement with any particular number.
